title: Remove init to zero for static variables
description:
The C standard requires that objects with static storage duration
is initialized to zero.

notes.body:
It's not illegal to init to zero, it's just not useful.
I'm not sure we should force this, but maybe give a warning?
Presumably it has a small effect on the size of the binary.  I did pause when seeing preference values that were previously set to false no longer explicitly initialised..

The compiler will handle init to zero just fine, but according to the C standard this is not needed. Do you have any concerns, other than code readability?

I'm fine with keeping the code without this modifications, but we do have a mix. My recent change for `hf_` and `ett_` variables also removed explicit init.
Yes, it was just the readability, but I am fine with this change.
We can always keep some init to zero if it improves readability, like for the preferences?
